name: WIMP model
description: Windows, Icons, Menus, Pointer paradigm originating from Xerox PARC that organized computing around pre-authored graphical interfaces, splitting users into programmers (who issue procedures) and everyone else (who choose from menus of pre-built actions)

edges.quote: the successor to WIMP is probably not "chat," at least not in the simplistic sense people sometimes mean... fixed graphical interfaces stop being the only sensible contract between user and machine once the user can increasingly express procedures through a model
not the end of interfaces, but the end of the assumption that interfaces must be fully fixed in advance because users cannot program the machine
